title: Convergence Without Finite Exactness in the Eigenstate Quantum Bootstrap
abstract: The eigenstate quantum-mechanical bootstrap can converge to the physical moment set while remaining nonexact at every finite order. We prove this for a one-dimensional quasi-exactly solvable sextic oscillator at explicitly known eigenvalues, including excited levels. At every finite order, the lower and upper bounds on $u^2$ remain strictly below and above its physical value, even after adjoining arbitrary finite polynomial Gram tests and all eigenstate-annihilator relations visible in the retained moment space. Hence neither side of the centered observable admits a finite sum-of-squares certificate modulo the eigenstate annihilator. The gap persists under any finite set of additional localizing constraints whose weights are strictly positive on polynomial vectors. We then prove convergence for polynomial Schrödinger operators satisfying explicit sum-of-squares confinement and derivative bounds. The eigenstate relations give moment estimates uniform in the truncation order; these yield a regular Schrödinger representation supported on the prescribed eigenspace. Finally, a four-mode extension combines this fixed-observable obstruction with feasible position moments having no positive representing measure at every finite order. At level three, this construction yields nonphysical feasible points with strictly positive definite moment matrices.
summary: This paper rigorously examines the eigenstate quantum-mechanical bootstrap, demonstrating that even when moment constraints converge to the physical spectrum, they do so without ever achieving exactness at any finite computational step. Using a sextic oscillator as a key example, the authors show that persistent gaps exist between the calculated bounds and the true physical value. This highlights fundamental limitations in using finite moment data to fully characterize quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the convergence properties of the eigenstate quantum-mechanical bootstrap method when applied to determining physical quantum spectra.
main_result: It proves that the bootstrap can converge to the physical moment set without achieving exactness at any finite computational order, demonstrating persistent gaps between finite bounds and the true physical value.
method: The analysis employs moment methods, semidefinite programming (SDP) constraints derived from operator identities, and functional analysis on the Weyl algebra to constrain quantum expectation values.
model_or_system: The primary model analyzed is a one-dimensional quasi-exactly solvable sextic oscillator, though the methods are generalized to confining polynomial Schrödinger operators.
key_observables: The centered observable $u^2$, and the moment bounds $\langle q^{2n}_j angle$ and $\langle p^{2n}_j angle$ for position and momentum.
important_parameters: The truncation order ($K$) of the moment space, and the physical energy eigenvalue ($e$).
main_assumptions: The convergence theorems rely on specific polynomial hypotheses (sum-of-squares conditions) being satisfied by the potential, and the analysis often involves assuming the existence of a compact resolvent.
figures_summary: The notes do not describe specific figures, but mention numerical tables showing the convergence of objective functions for different truncation orders ($K=3, 4, 5$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the non-exactness of finite bounds for the sextic oscillator, then proving uniform moment bounds for general confining potentials, and finally extending the analysis to show that the failure of finite exactness persists even with additional localizing constraints.
why_interesting: This work provides deep theoretical insights into the limitations of moment-based reconstruction techniques in quantum mechanics, which is crucial for understanding the robustness of spectral determination methods in quantum field theory and many-body physics.
